newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Shell, Occidental units sign pact with Manila firm.
newsitem.headline: Shell, Occidental units sign pact with Manila firm.

text.p: Shell Philippines Exploration and Occidental Philippines have signed a pact with a subsidiary of the state-run Philippine National Oil Co to begin negotiations for a possible venture in a gas pipeline project.

In a joint statement on Tuesday, Shell and Occidental who are developers of the Camago-Malampaya gas field, the biggest gas field in the country, said the memorandum of understanding was signed with the PNOC-Exploration Corp (PNOC-EC) on February 27.
Shell Philippines is the local exploration arm of the Royal Dutch/Shell group of companies while Occidental Philippines is a subsidiary of Occidental Petroleum Corp.
PNOC-EC president Rufino Bomasang told Reuters by phone the parties expect an agreement after six months of talks.

Shell and Occidental are set to construct, operate and maintain an offshore pipeline that will bring gas from the Camago-Malampaya field in Palawan, southwestern Philippines to markets in the northern island of Luzon.

The Camago-Malampaya field with estimated reserves of three trillion cubic feet is set to begin commercial production in the year 2001. The reserves will be able to sustain the daily requirements of a 3,000-megawatt power plant.
Under its service contract, Shell and Occidental are allowed to enter into one or more contracts for the construction of the gas pipeline.
